thread.title: Rally May Stall For Indonesia Stock Market

author: rttnews.com
title: Rally May Stall For Indonesia Stock Market
text:
The Indonesia stock market has moved higher in back-to-back trading days, advancing more than 75 points or 1.2 percent along the way. The Jakarta Composite Index now rests just beneath the 5,860-point plateau although it may be stuck in neutral on Thursday.
The global forecast for the Asian markets remains soft, with technology stocks likely to continue to weigh. The European and U.S. markets were down and the Asian bourses figure to follow that lead.
The JCI finished modestly higher on Wednesday following gains from the cement stocks and a mixed picture from the financial sector.
For the day, the index picked up 23.09 points or 0.40 percent to finish at 5,858.29 after trading between 5,851.79 and 5,896.80.
Among the actives, Bank Danamon Indonesia advanced 1.03 percent, while Bank Central Asia eased 0.10 percent, Bank Negara Indonesia collected 1.58 percent, Bank Mandiri fell 0.35 percent, Indocement surged 6.37 percent, Semen Indonesia soared 9.29 percent, United Tractors retreated 1.15 percent, Indofood perked 0.89 percent, Bumi Resources plunged 5.14 percent, Vale Indonesia tumbled 4.62 percent, Voksel Electric spiked 3.06 percent, Bukit Darmo Property perked 3.39 percent, Lotte Chemical climbed 1.86 percent, SLJ Global skidded 1.03 percent, XL Axiata added 0.94 percent, Bank Pan Indonesia shed 0.92 percent, Jasa Marga gained 0.26 percent, Indosat slid 1.85 percent and Bank MNC Internasional and Bank Rakyat Indonesia were unchanged.
The lead from Wall Street is negative as stocks fluctuated wildly on Wednesday after opening higher. The major averages pulled back firmly into negative territory before staging an unsuccessful recovery attempt in the afternoon.
The Dow shed 205.99 points or 0.81 while the NASDAQ lost 64.48 points or 0.90 percent to 7,136.47 and the S&P 500 fell 20.60 points or 0.76
Tech shares remained under pressure as Apple (AAPL) following a downgrade drop in iPhone sales next year.
 Waters suggested she would halt President Donald Trump's efforts to roll back banking regulations.
Crude oil futures managed to close on a positive note on Wednesday after 12 successive days of declines. Crude oil futures for December edged higher Wednesday and settled at $56.25 a barrel, gaining $0.56 or 1 percent for the session.
Closer to home, the central bank in Indonesia will wrap up its monetary policy meeting today and then announce its decision on interest rates. The central bank is widely expected to keep its benchmark lending rate unchanged at 5.75 percent.
Indonesia also will see October figures for imports, exports and trade balance. In September, imports were worth $15.06 billion and exports were at $14.83 billion for a trade deficit of $0.23 billion.
